title: Modern SQL Server Features
description: JSON, temporal tables, columnstore, change data capture, In-Memory OLTP, Agent jobs, full-text search, and graph tables — the features that separate SQL Server 2016 and later from older versions.
longDescription: Most production SQL Server work still revolves around tables, indexes, and T-SQL, but the platform has added a set of features that solve problems the relational model handles awkwardly: semi-structured JSON payloads, automatic row versioning with temporal tables, columnar analytics with columnstore, log-based change capture with CDC, latch-free hot tables with In-Memory OLTP, scheduled automation with SQL Server Agent, linguistic search with full-text indexes, and many-to-many relationships with graph tables. This module teaches each feature with runnable T-SQL, the trade-offs that matter in production, and the interview questions that reveal whether you have used them or only read about them.
whatYouLearn: Store, validate, query, and index JSON documents with JSON_VALUE, OPENJSON, and FOR JSON
Keep automatic row history with system-versioned temporal tables and query it with FOR SYSTEM_TIME
Choose between clustered, nonclustered, and ordered columnstore indexes for analytics
Capture inserts, updates, and deletes with Change Data Capture and consume the change table
Use memory-optimized tables and natively compiled procedures for high-contention workloads
Create and monitor SQL Server Agent jobs with schedules, retries, and history queries
Build full-text indexes and use CONTAINS, FREETEXT, and CONTAINSTABLE effectively
Model many-to-many relationships with NODE and EDGE tables and query them with MATCH
